modules.name: AshReXcue BootLoop Protector
modules.author: AshBorn (@Ripper_Hybrid)
modules.description: 🔰 Your safety net for bad modules. Catches boot loops, disables the culprits.
modules.readme:
AshReXcue - Bootloop Protector

📖 About

AshReXcue (formerly AshLooper) is a sophisticated, open-source boot protection module designed for Magisk, KernelSU, APatch, and their various Forks.

Unlike basic protectors that blindly disable all modules during a bootloop, AshReXcue utilizes Smart Differential Analysis to identify and target only the problematic modules and service.d boot scripts. It features a fully interactive, locally hosted WebUI Dashboard for managing your protection parameters, reviewing boot logs, and configuring system behaviors offering a completely local experience with no cumbersome login processes or external dependencies.

📚 Read The Full Feature Documentation

Partition Backup: AshReXcue can optionally backup critical partitions during installation. See the Feature Documentation for supported partitions, how to request additional ones, and safety considerations.

✨ Core Architecture

| Category | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| 🔰 Smart Detection | Differential tracking (hash + size + status) detects exactly what changed since the last successful boot to isolate bad modules and boot scripts, backed by aggressive framework process monitoring (3-strike restart threshold). |
| 📜 Boot Script Guard | Optionally tracks and protects service.d scripts the same way it protects modules, isolating offenders into a recovery vault instead of deleting them outright. |
| 💻 Interactive WebUI | A self-hosted localhost dashboard (V2.7) featuring a claymorphic/neumorphic dark aesthetic, a unified Items control center, a global unsaved-changes tracker, and built-in diagnostics (Activity Log + JSON Viewer). |
| 🔒 Secure Environment | Built-in security measures including strict /proc/net/tcp port collision checks, decoupled static monitor.sh background tracking, and hash-based local authentication. |
| ⚙️ Customizable Logic | Highly configurable thresholds, dynamic stability timeframes, toggleable extra daemon checks, and intelligent crash-reboot cycling with active state-locks to prevent race conditions. |
| 📝 Access Control | A unified Whitelist Manager covering both modules and boot scripts, plus a dedicated Items tab to pause, restore, or permanently remove any tracked item. |

📥 Installation

Install via your preferred root manager (Magisk, KernelSU, or APatch).

The module features an interactive installation process made up of five steps. Follow the on-screen prompts and use the volume keys to configure your baseline protection settings.
Installer Controls:
- Vol+ = Select / confirm the highlighted option
- Vol- = Move to the next option

During installation, AshReXcue walks you through an interactive setup so you can choose your protection mode, loop threshold, script monitoring, optional stability checks, and optional partition backup. Those choices can be changed later in the WebUI or the local Action Menu.

*Note: All settings configured during installation can be modified dynamically at any time via the WebUI or the local Action Menu.*

🖥️ Accessing the Dashboard & Action Menu

AshReXcue features an interactive CLI-based Action Menu powered by a shared volume-key and touch listener. This serves as the central hub for managing the module. From this 5-option menu, you can securely launch the WebUI on localhost, add/remove items from your Whitelist, restore previously disabled modules/scripts, or safely exit.

You can access this menu dynamically based on your root manager:

Method 1: Root Manager UI (KernelSU / APatch)
Simply tap the "WebUI" or "Action" button directly within your module manager application to spawn the interactive menu.

Method 2: Magisk & Universal
Tap the "Action" button directly within the Magisk module menu. This seamlessly executes the module's built-in action.sh script, launching the interactive Action Menu right on your screen.

📁 Important Notices

Infrastructure Redundancy details

Mirrors & Updates
- Primary: GitHub Releases
- Mirror: GitLab Repository

Compatibility
Do not use this module alongside other bootloop protection modules. Running multiple bootloop protectors at the same time can conflict and may cause serious boot issues.

🤝 Credits
- jq Binary – jqlang.org - The engine behind the JSON differential analysis.
- zip Binary – Info-ZIP - Used for partition backup ZIP creation.
- Cloudflare – Pages - Reliable hosting infrastructure.

👤 Author
- AshBorn - @Ripper_Hybrid
modules.changelog:
🚀 AshReXcue v10.1 Update Changelog

🔰 Core Engine
- Framework Watchdog: Now tracks the core framework processes by PID instead of only SystemUI, and treats three framework restarts in one boot as a loop.
- No Double-Counting: A parent restart re-baselines its children, so one framework restart no longer counts as several crashes.
- Property Read Guard: If system properties can't be read three checks in a row, the watchdog turns itself off for that boot instead of forcing a reboot.
- Extra Stability Scope: Turning on Extra Stability now also watches servicemanager and vold for restarts.
- Service.d Only: Script monitoring now covers only service.d scripts; post-mount.d and post-fs-data.d scripts are no longer tracked or auto-disabled.
- Settings Sanitizing: Invalid or out-of-range values are reset to defaults at boot and when the WebUI opens.

📲 Installer
- Binary Check: Setup verifies the bundled jq and zip are present and runnable, aborting with a clear message instead of installing a broken module.
- Saved Config Check: A restored stability window outside the allowed range now falls back to the default with a notice.

🎨 WebUI
- Stability Window: Watch time is now limited to 45–90 seconds with a 60 second default, and the stepper refuses values outside that range.
- Real Command Status: The WebUI now receives each command's real exit code, so failed commands show as errors instead of silent successes.
- Activity Log Export: Saving the log to Downloads now handles quotes, newlines or $, which used to break the save.

zaprett

О модуле
Представляет собой портированную версию zapret от bol-van для Android устройств.

Какую версию модуля выбрать?

В актуальных релизах есть 2 версии модуля, а именно:
- zaprett.zip
- zaprett-hosts.zip (с /etc/hosts)

Что такое /etc/hosts?
Говоря грубо, это файл, который влияет на работу нейросетей и других недоступных сервисов, перенаправляя ваш траффик на сторонние сервера.

Если вы используете модули, которые подменяют этот файл (например, всевозможные блокировщики рекламы и разблокировщики нейросетей), выбирайте версию без hosts, иначе модули будут конфликтовать друг с другом.

modules.name: Yet Another Bootloop Protector
modules.author: rhythmcache.t.me
modules.description: This module try to detect and fix bootloops caused by Magisk modules.
modules.readme:
Yet Another Bootloop Protector.
- This module try to protect your device from bootloops and system ui failures caused by Magisk/KernelSU/APatch Modules.
- Generally , This Module can fix these type of bootloops if their cause is Magisk Modules.
  1)  The device repeatedly restarts but may show the boot animation  before crashing and restarting again.
  2)  The device gets stuck at the boot animation and never progresses to the lock screen.
  3)  device boots successfully, but SystemUI fails to start, causing a black or unresponsive screen."

Installation
- Flash it in Magisk,KSU or Apatch
- if you flash it in custom recovery , it will disable all the magisk/KSU/APatch modules for no reason. Flash it in TWRP only when necessary.

 ### Bootloop
- If a bootloop is detected, , it will automatically disable every Magisk/KSU/APatch module and set the permissions of all general scripts (scripts placed in /data/adb/service.d , /data/adb/post-fs-data.d /data/adb/post-mount.d and /data/adb/boot-completed.d) to 644
- You can manually enable each module, or you can use the action button. Using the action button will also set executable permissions chmod +x for all general scripts

Recovery
- Flashing this module in TWRP or custom recoveries will automatically disable all Magisk/KSU/APatch modules and general scripts. Your data partition should be accessible otherwise, it won't work.
- It may not work with all recoveries.

How does it work?
• Each time the device fails to complete the boot, the module creates a "marker"
- No marker files: it creates the first marker (marker1).
- One marker file: it creates a second marker (marker2).
- Two marker files: it creates a third marker (marker3).
- When three markers are present, the module considers the device to be in a boot loop , and  it disables all Magisk modules by creating a disable file in each module's folder. This action prevents those modules from loading during the next boot, which may help the device boot correctly.
- The module waits for the boot to complete, checking every 5 seconds.
If the boot does not complete within a set timeout period (2 minutes by default), the module assumes there is a boot problem, disables all Magisk modules and general scrips, and reboots the device.
- The module also monitors the state of zygote during booting and disables all modules if unusual behavior is detected.

  ### whitelist
- you can add module-id to /data/adb/YABP/allowed-modules.txt ,and script names to allowed-scripts.txt, those scripts/modules wont be disabled even if a bootloop is detected

SystemUI Monitor (optional)
- some modules, especially customization modules, may sometimes cause SystemUI to crash. Enabling this could help in tracking and resolving such issues.
- You will be prompted to disable or enable system ui monitor while installing the module.
- if enabled , then The Module checks the status of the SystemUI process every 5 seconds.
- If SystemUI is not running, the module starts tracking it and if SystemUI remains inactive for more than 25  seconds , or if it crashes too often the module assumes a failure of the device and it disables all the magisk modules and general scripts and triggers a reboot
- To  disable the systemUi Monitor , you can create a file named systemui.monitor.disable in /data/adb or you can just run
su -c touch /data/adb/systemui.monitor.disable
to enable the systemui monitor , you can just remove that file, or you can run , (changes will take place after the next boot)
su -c rm -f /data/adb/systemui.monitor.disable
- Logs of this module will be found at /data/local/tmp/service.log
- you can run rm -f /data/local/tmp/service.log to clear the logs.

Limitations
- If the cause of the bootloop is not related to Magisk/KSU/APatch modules, this module won't help.
- If any modules directly modify system files, this module won't help.
- In cases where a module uses an incompatible system.prop or causes a bootloop during the early boot stages (post-fs-data), this module may not be able to disable it in time.
In these cases , you can always flash it in TWRP to disable Modules

Support Me

Hii! I'm rhythmcache, the developer of YetAnotherBootloopProtector.

If you like this project, consider supporting me by sponsoring the project or buying me a coffee. It really helps me continue working on it!

modules.readme:
Magic ToolFlash

An android CLI flash tool without custom recoveries. Usage in Terminal Emulator or Termux with Root access:
flash [ZIP...]

If some zips fail to flash, you can try:

export NOSYSTEM=1; flash [ZIP...]

Path to ZIP should be full and multiple ZIP at same time are allowed. Busybox must be installed!!

Flash will not be processed in Android environment. Instead, Magic FlashTool will create a new environment and flashing will be performed in isolated chroot environment to match with Custom Recovery environment.

IMPORTANT: Only use this for flashing mods zip. It can be magisk module, magisk app, system mods zip, ... Do not use this tool to flash ROM while Android system is running because it will lead to bootloop

For testing, you can open shell in chroot enviroment with this command:

vmshell

Known issues
- (Solved) ~~The flashable zip that uses /tmp as temporary directory will not work as /tmp does not exist on Android root directory. Please prefer to use /dev/tmp as temporary directory.~~
- (Solved) ~~The flashable zip hardcoded /sbin in command might not work because /sbin doesn't always exist on Android 11+~~

modules.readme:
OpenList Magisk/KernelSU/APatch 模块
第一次用？先看 安装包与更新通道说明 —— 5 个包怎么选、两条更新通道有什么区别，都在那里。
许可提示：本模块的脚本、WebUI 与文档使用 MIT 许可；安装包内打包的 OpenList 可执行文件（openlist-arm / openlist-arm64）来自上游 OpenListTeam/OpenList，使用 AGPL-3.0。两者许可不同，分发前请先看 THIRD-PARTY.md。

OpenList Magisk 模块将 OpenList 文件服务器集成到 Android 系统中，通过 Magisk、KernelSU 或 APatch 以系统化方式运行，支持 ARM 和 ARM64 架构。

功能亮点

安装
- 三种二进制位置：/data/adb/openlist/bin、模块 bin/、模块 system/bin
- 两种数据目录：/data/adb/openlist、/sdcard/Android/openlist
- 更新安装时如果换了数据目录，可以顺手把旧数据迁过来（音量+ 迁移 / 音量- 跳过，默认跳过）
- 管理员账号交给网页向导创建，安装脚本不碰密码

运行
- 三家框架通用：Magisk / KernelSU / APatch，同一份 control.sh
- 开机自启：先等 sys.boot_completed，再等外部存储可写，/sdcard 挂载慢的机器也不会失败
- 自动识别访问地址：优先取默认路由的 src，避开 172.16–31 这类虚拟网卡

WebUI（KernelSU / APatch）
- 状态、启停、重启、打开网页
- 路径体检：列出所有二进制与数据目录，清理多余副本、切换、删除
- 所有版本：官方 Release 全列表，任意版本升级或回退
- 在线更新：可选下载镜像、显示下载进度、启动失败自动回滚
- 下载配置、管理员账号、存储、离线任务、日志、迁移
- 毛玻璃 + 大圆角，自动 / 浅色 / 深色主题

命令行
- control.sh 覆盖全部功能，Magisk 用户在终端直接调

截图展示

| 模块界面 | 安装完成 |
|---|---|
|  |  |

| 在线下载二进制 | 数据迁移 |
|---|---|
|  |  |

WebUI 全页（KernelSU / APatch 模块页面里的控制台）

系统要求
- Android 设备，支持 arm / arm64 / x86 / x86_64 四种架构
- Magisk v20.4 以上、KernelSU 或 APatch，任选其一
- Root 权限

安装包怎么选

一共 5 个包，分两个更新通道。按架构挑一个装，以后它就自己跟着自己那条通道更新。

| 包名 | 内含二进制 | 体积 | 适合谁 |
|---|---|---|---|
| openlist-magisk-vX-arm64.zip | arm64 | ~58 MB | 绝大多数手机，首选 |
| openlist-magisk-vX-arm.zip | arm | ~60 MB | 只有 arm32 的老设备 |
| openlist-magisk-vX-amd64.zip | amd64 | ~58 MB | x86_64 设备（WSA、部分掌机） |
| openlist-magisk-vX-386.zip | 386 | ~59 MB | x86 设备（模拟器） |
| openlist-magisk-online.zip | 无 | ~76 KB | 想省流量，安装时现下（~55 MB） |

两条通道的版本号体系完全独立，所以各自占一个 Release：架构包用上游版本号（v4.2.10），online 用日期版本号（2026.11.24-1）。装哪个包就跟哪条通道，互不影响。

装错了也不会坏：包里没有当前架构的二进制时，安装脚本会自动去下载，见下一节。

两条更新通道

| 通道 | 包内 updateJson | 模块版本号 | versionCode 规则 | 更新日志 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 架构通道（arm64 / arm / amd64 / 386） | update-.json | 跟随 OpenList 二进制 | 主×10000 + 次×100 + 修订 | 上游 CHANGELOG |
| 在线通道（online） | update.json | 日期 + 当日流水号（2026.11.24-1） | Unix 日数 × 100 + (流水号-1) | CHANGELOG-ONLINE.md |

装的是哪个包，模块管理器就检查哪条通道，两者互不干扰 —— 上游发新版不会把 online 用户的版本号顶掉，反过来也一样。

online 包是什么：提前体验版

openlist-magisk-online.zip 和其它 4 个包是同一个模块的两种装法，注册名分别是 OpenList(online) 和 OpenList(binary)。

| | OpenList(binary)（arm64 / arm / amd64 / 386） | OpenList(online) |
|---|---|---|
| 谁发版 | CI 全自动 | 我手动触发 |
| 跟着谁走 | 上游 OpenList 官方 Release | 模块自身的脚本 / WebUI 改动 |
| 什么时候更新 | 上游发新版才更新 | 模块功能改了就发 |
| 包内二进制 | 自带，离线可装 | 无，安装时下载约 55 MB |
| 版本号 | 跟随 OpenList（如 v4.2.10） | 日期 + 流水号（如 2026.11.24-1） |

要点：
- online 是提前体验版。 模块的安装脚本、WebUI、控制逻辑改了什么，我手动发一版 online，装了它的用户立刻用上，不用等上游 OpenList 发新版。
- 代价是包里没有二进制。 装的时候要联网下载对应架构的二进制（约 55 MB），或者装完在 WebUI 里点「立即更新」。断网装不了，除非提前把 openlist-android-.tar.gz 放进 Download 目录。
- 4 个架构包全自动，我不插手。 CI 只盯上游 OpenList 的 Release，上游一发就自动构建、自动发版，二进制版本号跟模块版本号严格对齐。
- 所以架构包用户拿不到我新改的模块功能，得等上游下次发版。想提前用，改装 online 包 —— 之后你的更新就跟着 online 通道走，不会自动切回架构通道；想回去就重装一个架构包。

两套版本号互不干扰：online 是 2026.11.24-1、2026.11.24-2…（日期 + 当日第几版，次日归零），架构包是 v4.2.10、v4.2.11…（跟 OpenList 走）。versionCode 用不同算法，不会互相判成降级。

二进制获取顺序

customize.sh 按下面四级回退，任一成功就停：

1. 包内二进制 $MODROOT/openlist- —— 4 个架构包走这条
2. Download 目录 /sdcard/Download/openlist-android-.tar.gz —— 提前放好就能离线装
3. 在线下载 —— 调 control.sh fetch-bin  ，直连 + 15 个国内镜像依次试，带 md5 校验
4. 全失败 —— abort 并打印手动下载地址与放置路径

在线下载优先走上游固定版本路径（releases/download//），不消耗 GitHub API 额度、不需要 token。架构包传下去的版本号就是上游版本，拿到的是严格对应的那一版；online 包传的是日期版本号，上游没有这个 tag，会先探测、再自动回退到上游 latest。
TWRP/recovery 里刷机且断网时，先按第 2 条把 openlist-android-.tar.gz 拷进 Download 目录，再刷 online 包也能装上。

框架兼容性

| 框架 | 模块系统 | 动作按钮 | 更新机制 | WebUI |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Magisk | ✅ v20.4+ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ 用「操作」按钮或终端 |
| KernelSU | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| APatch | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |

三家跑的是同一份 control.sh，行为一致，只是入口不同。卸载脚本会从 service.sh 读真实路径，迁到自定义目录也能清干净。

安装步骤

1. 下载模块
- 从 GitHub Releases 挑一个包（见 安装包怎么选）
- ARM64 设备拿 openlist-magisk-vX-arm64.zip 就行；不确定架构可以用 openlist-magisk-online.zip（约 76 KB，安装时自动识别并下载）

2. 安装配置
- 打开 Magisk 管理器、KernelSU 管理器 或 APatch 管理器
- 选择"从本地安装"
- 进入安装配置界面：
- 选择二进制文件安装位置
- 选择数据目录存储位置
- 更新安装时如果检测到旧数据，会多问一句要不要一起迁过来
- 包里没有对应架构的二进制时会自动在线下载，装的时候别断网

3. 完成安装
- 等待安装完成
- 重启设备

使用说明

服务管理
- 开机自动启动：late_start 阶段先等 sys.boot_completed（最多 120 秒），数据目录在 /sdcard 或 /storage 时再等它可写（最多 180 秒），然后才拉起服务
- 管理器里点「操作」按钮（action.sh）可手动启停
- 状态写在 module.prop 的 description 里：运行时显示地址和 PID，停止时显示提示

WebUI 控制台

| 区块 | 能做什么 |
|---|---|
| 状态 | 运行中/已停止、地址、PID；启停、重启、打开网页 |
| 目录 | 模块目录、数据目录、二进制路径，点击复制 |
| 路径体检 | 3 个二进制位置 + 2 个数据目录的占用；清理多余副本、切换数据目录、删除非当前目录 |
| 所有版本 | 全部 Release（含历史），一键升级或回退 |
| 版本与更新 | 检查更新、立即更新：后台下载、进度可见、起不来自动回滚 |
| 下载镜像 | 自动选择 / 直连 / 15 个国内镜像 / 自定义；自动模式按实测延迟排序 |
| 下载配置 | 端口、Token、目标路径、离线引擎、删除策略、预设路径 |
| 管理员账号 | 改用户名、改密码（走管理 API，在线生效，不重启） |
| 存储 | 列表、启用、禁用、全部重载 |
| 离线任务 | 进行中任务、进度、取消 |
| 迁移 | 数据目录 / 二进制点选迁移，迁移 = 移动（校验通过才删源） |
| 日志 | 「服务日志 / 程序输出」两页 |

访问方式
- Web 界面访问：http://:5244
- 首次打开会进入安装向导，按提示设置管理员账号和密码
- 完成向导前，WebUI 里存储、离线任务、设置会提示「还没有管理员账号」

数据存储
- 默认数据目录：/data/adb/openlist/，日志是同目录下的 service.log 和 openlist.log
- 下载镜像偏好存在 /mirror.conf，跟着数据目录走，模块更新不会丢
- 卸载默认保留数据：只清理二进制。确实要连数据一起删，卸载前执行
  touch /data/adb/modules/openlist/.delete_data_on_uninstall，或卸载后手动 rm -rf

数据迁移说明
1. 安装时可选择数据目录与二进制位置
2. 装好后也能在 WebUI 迁移页随时改：选目标目录 → 「开始迁移」
3. 迁移 = 移动：复制、校验文件数与 data.db 的 md5 全部通过后，才同步 config.json 路径并删除源目录
4. 二进制迁移同理，校验一致后删除旧文件，不会同时留两份
5. 迁移完成后 WebUI 自动刷新状态、路径体检与日志

故障排除

常见问题
1. 无法访问服务
- 检查网络连接
- 检查服务状态：pgrep -f openlist
- 查看日志文件
- 手动重启服务：su -c /data/adb/modules/openlist/service.sh

2. IP 地址获取失败
- 确认 WiFi 或移动网络已连接
- 检查网络接口状态
- 查看模块日志

3. 服务无法启动
- 检查二进制文件权限
- 确认数据目录可写
- 查看详细日志

4. 检查更新没反应 / 更新失败
- 提示「GitHub 不可达，显示的是缓存版本」属于正常降级，版本列表来自上次缓存
- 更新失败现在会带原因（error= 或退出码），日志页看 service.log
- 国内直连 api.github.com 经常不通，可把 PAT 写进模块目录 .github_token（额度 60 → 5000 次/小时）
- 下载走镜像：「下载镜像」里选「自动选择」，或指定某个镜像

5. 重启后没有自动启动
- 看 /data/adb/modules/openlist/service.log 最后几行
- 卡在「等待外部存储就绪」是 /sdcard 挂载慢，最多等 180 秒，不用管
- 手动跑一次确认二进制的数据目录没问题：su -c /data/adb/modules/openlist/service.sh

6. WebUI 打不开
- Magisk 没有 WebUI 机制，只能用「操作」按钮或终端 control.sh
- KernelSU / APatch 在模块卡片里点 WebUI

7. online 包装不上 / 提示缺少二进制
- 这个包不含二进制，安装时要联网下载（约 55 MB），断网就会中止...
modules.changelog:
OpenList(online) 说明与更新日志

模块显示名 OpenList(online)，安装包 openlist-magisk-online.zip，包里不含任何二进制。
版本号说明
- online 的版本号用日期 + 当日流水号，形如 2026.11.24-1、2026.11.24-2，每天从 -1 起，第二天归零。
- 同一个日期重复发布时，CI 读 update.json 里的上一版自动把流水号 +1，你只需要填 8 位日期（如 20261124）。
- versionCode = Unix 日数 × 100 + (流水号 - 1)，例：2026.11.24-1 → 2078100，2026.11.24-2 → 2078101。跨天比较也严格递增，不会把新版判成降级。
- online 的版本号不跟随上游 OpenList 的版本号 —— 因为本包不含二进制，安装时下载的是最新版，写死某个上游版本号会变成假的。OpenList 二进制是哪个版本，请在模块 WebUI 里查看。
- 4 个架构包的显示名是 OpenList(binary)，版本号依然跟随 OpenList 二进制版本，由 CI 自动同步。

和另外 4 个包的区别

| | OpenList(online) | OpenList(binary) |
|---|---|---|
| 安装包 | openlist-magisk-online.zip | openlist-magisk-vX-.zip |
| 内含二进制 | 无 | 对应架构的那一份 |
| 模块版本号 | 日期 + 当日流水号（2026.11.24-1），发布时只填日期 | 跟随 OpenList 二进制版本 |
| versionCode | Unix 日数 × 100 + (流水号-1) | 主×10000 + 次×100 + 修订 |
| 更新检查 | 仓库 update.json | 各自的 update-.json |
| 谁发版 | 手动 | CI 跟着上游 OpenList 自动发 |
| 更新内容 | 模块自身（脚本 / WebUI / 安装逻辑） | 模块 + 上游新版本二进制 |

两套更新清单互不共用：online 只看 update.json，架构包只看自己的 update-arm64.json 之类。装哪个就跟哪条通道，不会互相顶掉版本号。

这个包更新的是模块，不是上游 OpenList
- 装了 OpenList(online) 的用户优先体验模块新功能：脚本、WebUI、安装逻辑改了什么，手动发一版就能用上，不用等上游 OpenList 发新版。
- 4 个架构包相反：只有上游 OpenList 发布新版本，CI 才自动构建，root 管理器才会提示更新。
- online 版本不跟随 CI，它只跟模块自身的改动。

想更新 OpenList 二进制怎么办

OpenList(online) 里没有二进制，所以它有两条独立的更新路径：

1. 重装一次 online 包 —— 安装时会按设备架构自动获取最新版本的 OpenList 二进制，顺带带上最新的模块文件。
2. root 管理器的 WebUI —— 在模块的 WebUI 里可以单独升级或回退 OpenList 二进制，不影响模块本身。

这个日志长期不变，说明模块没有更新

正常情况下，没有 issue 或 bug 修复，online 会长期保持不更新——因为模块本身没什么可改的。这是设计如此，不是出问题了：
- 想拿上游 OpenList 的新版本 → 用 4 个架构包（OpenList(binary)），它们会跟着官方发布，在 root 管理器里提示更新。
- 想拿模块的新功能 → 看这个日志有没有新条目。

2026.11.24-1

首个纯在线包，也是改用「日期 + 流水号」后的第一版（versionCode 2078100）。
- 模块显示名 OpenList(online)，不再叫 Magisk / KernelSU / APatch 模块
- 安装包不含二进制，安装时按设备架构（arm / arm64 / amd64 / 386）自动下载对应版本
- 下载走固定的版本路径，并用上游 md5-android.txt 校验
- 直连失败自动切 15 个国内镜像，全部失败才中止，并打印手动下载地址与放置路径
- 也支持提前把 openlist-android-.tar.gz 放进 Download 目录离线安装
- 模块版本号在上游不存在时（本包用的是 1.x），自动改用上游最新版本的二进制，不会因为版本对不上而 404
这个版本目前只有纯在线包；架构包会等上游 OpenList 发布同版本后由 CI 自动补上。

Nano for Android NDK
osm0sis @ xda-developers
*Static arm/arm64 nano binary for Android built with the NDK*

Links
- GitHub
- Support
- Sponsor
- Donate

Description
An installer to push my own static Android arm/arm64 build of the nano editor and required files to /system/xbin/ and /system/etc/terminfo/, with a wrapper adding a --term option to try terminfo profiles more easily. Detects and supports SuperSU/Magisk systemless installs. Can then be used from Terminal while booted.

When flashed in recovery also allows temporary recovery use by pushing a script to /sbin/nano with the required setup, so you can trigger it from adb shell or TWRP Terminal. Makes it extremely easy and worry-free to tweak and mod on the go, knowing you can edit the faulty build.prop or startup script if something goes wrong.

modules.readme:
gboard_dict_3

modules.name: Hifi Maximizer
modules.author: zyhk
modules.description: A module for maximizing the digital audio fidelity by reducing jitters on audio outputs (USB DACs, Bluetooth a2dp, DLNA, etc.)
modules.readme:
A Magisk module for maximizing the digital audio fidelity by reducing jitters on audio outputs (USB DACs, Bluetooth a2dp, DLNA, etc.)

So many music lovers abandon audio quality on smart phones and DAP's by believing its causes are delivered from analog components. However, the most crucial cuase of it is actually less than 50 Hz jitter (i.e., the standard deviation of actual audio data rate with a low-pass filter; usually converting into time-domain) on digital audio outputs that generates very short reverb or foggy sound like distortion on analog audio outputs. Although larger than 50 Hz (shorter than 20 msec. interval) jitter can be easily reduced under the hearable level by a PLL (Phase Locked Loop) in DAC's, the other (especially less than 10 Hz or longer than 100 msec. interval) modulates and distorts audio outputs by fluctuating the master clock in a DAC through the PLL. For further explanation, see my another magisk module "Audio jitter silencer".

For maximizing the audio fidelity, this module reduces less than 50 Hz (longer than 20 msec interval) jitters on digital audio outputs by optimizing kenel tunables (CPU & GPU  governors, thermal control, CPU hotplug, I/O scheduler, Virtual memory), Selinux mode, WIFI parameters, etc. as follows,
- For Reducing Jitters:

    CPU & GPU governor
        change their governors to "performance" (additionally fixed at the max frequency).
    I/O scheduler
        scheduler preference: "deadline" ("cfq" if "deadline" doesn't exist); optimize its tunables.
    Virtual memory
        change "swappiness" to 0%, "laptop mode" to 1, etc.
    Thermal Control
        disable Qcomm "core control" and stop thermal servers (e.g., "thermald", "thermal-engine", "thermal", "mi_thermald", etc.).
    CPU hotplug
        stop "MPDecision" server (if exists).
    Disable MediaTek EAS+ scheduler
            Doze
        stop the Android doze server.
    Selinux mode
        change the mode to "permissive".
    Adaptive battery saving features
        disable wifi suspend optimizations, the adaptive battery management, the adaptive charging management and the adaptive connectivity management.
    Kill effect chains
        force ignoring     Disable the android built-in spatial audio feature (A13 or higher; especially Tensor devices)
         bypass an otiose audio pass.
    Disable aocd service
        disable "aocd server" generating significant jitter on audio outputs, esp. on USB.
    Disable pre-installed Moto Dolby and Digital Wellbeing features
        hide their apps (no modifications); please manually uninstall Digital Wellbeing app if remaining as a usual app.
    Disable Logd service
        disable "logd server", "traced server" and "traced_probes server" interfering jitter on audio outputs.
    Disable camera service
        disable "camera server" interfering jitter on audio outputs.
- For Convenience and Audio Quality:

     Disable DRC (Dynamic Range Control, i.e., a kind of compression)
        modify     Volume steps
        change the number of steps in media volume to 100 steps (0.4~0.7dB per step).
    Disables the sound dose feature of the mixer
        Not to defocuse the shape of sound images, also reduce jitter.
    Resampling quality
        change AudioFlinger's resampling quality from the AOSP standard one (stop band attenuation 90dB & cut off 100% of the Nyquist frequency & half filter length 32) to a very mastering quality (194dB & 98% & 520, 179dB & 99% & 408, 167dB & 106% & 368 or 160db & 91% & 480 (or 320 for low performance devices), i.e., no resampling distortion in a real sense even though the 160dB targeted attenuation is not accomplished in the AOSP implementation). However, install "Resampling for cheapies" module together to override these resampling settings if you intend to use LDAC bluetooth earphones or DAC's under $30.
    Adjust a USB transfer period of the USB HAL driver (not the Qcomm hardware offload USB driver, but including ones of Tensor and MTK devices)
        for directly reducing the jitter of a PLL in a DAC (even in an asynchronous mode); Use "USB_SampleRate_Changer" or "Audio Samplerate Changer" to switch from the usual hardware offload USB driver to the USB HAL one.
    Set an audio scheduling tunable "vendor.audio.adm.buffering.ms" "2"
         to reduce jitter on all audio outputs.
    Nullify volume listener libraries in "soundfx" folders  for disabling slight compression (maybe a peak limiter only on Qcomm devices).
    Set 192kHz & 32bit mode (max., but automatic for lower capability DAC's) for all the USB audio outputs (including non- Hi-Res audio tracks) of Tensor devices exceptionally
         because Tensor devices lower audio quality extremely for lower sample rates and bit depths, though the quality of in-DAC over-sampling filters is much worse than that of the re-sampling filter used by this module and the filters lower the quality particularly for input of lower sample rates as usual.
- Don't forget to install "Audio jitter silencer" together and uninstall "Digital Wellbeing" app (for reducing very large jitters which this module cannot reduce by itself)! And uninstall "Audio misc. settings" and "DRC remover" if they have already been installed, because all their functions are included in this module. Additionally if your device uses a Tensor SoC, uninstall "USB Samplerate Unlocker" for the same reason.
- Don't use Am@zon music using a much worse internal re-sampler which bypasses the mastering quality re-sampling in the OS mixer (audioFlinger). Other music streaming services don't use such an internal re-sampler, as far as I know.
- This module has been tested on LineageOS and crDroid ROM's, and phh GSI's (Android 10 ~ 16, Qualcomm & MediaTek SoC, and Arm32 & Arm64 combinations). For users of Motorola and Xiaomi stock ROM's, try to install a GSI through DSU and this module together once, then you could know how much the ROM's degrade audio quality probably for adapting to regulations....
modules.changelog:
- Tuned I/O scheduling parameters for Pixel 8's and Pixel 6's
- Dropped a USB offload driver support for Pixel 6's (now supported by a USB HAL driver up to 768kHz only).

This is the first release tuned for Pixel 8's and perhaps other recent Pixel series. Enjoy Bluetooth LDAC sound of highest quality on Pixel 8's!

However, because AIDL only devices like Pixel 7, 8, 9, 10's cannot use my USB audio up-sampling module or script tool till now, you may need a USB DAC with a "minimum phase" interpolator as default or selectable, e.g. CS43131, CS43198, KT20H20, etc. for avoiding pre-echo. Non-AIDL only devices having "audio_policy_configuration.xml" don't need such a DAC because by using my up-sampling module or script tool hearable pre-echo and post-echo aren't generated when up-sampling.

Lastly, don't forget installing "Audio Jitter Silencer" module to reduce digital distortion generated by your phone's battery saving features.

modules.name: AINUR 💎 SILMARIL
modules.author: UltraM8, Zackptg5
modules.description: Unleash the true scale of iridescent high-fidelity audioscapes and enchant music with celestial splendor for all playback & connectivity types.
modules.readme:
AINUR SILMARIL

SILMARIL is latest android audio modification installment in AINUR AUDIO series. Named after Silmarils - JRR Tolkien's legendarium light-embodying gems. SILMARIL stays true to its legendary namesake, encapsulating the luminous essence of sound: vivid, nuanced, rapid, grand & deeply emotional. Dedicated to bring high-fidelity true-res audio to a wide range of devices - SILMARIL adaptive design scales across various platforms, including Qualcomm, MediaTek, and Google Tensor, ensuring optimal audio output tailored to each device. Its ability to support an extensive range of playback options, ensures that whether you're using heaphones, external DACs, streaming services, or dedicated music player - music comes at an awe glory. SILMARIL elevates the audio experience to new heights, pushing boundaries and transforming the device into a vessel that sails through immersive sound waves.
### Dynamic Installer
SILMARIL dynamically checks software/hardware environment context it's getting installed on to determine content to edit. This, further backed up by patches being corrected against respective sources, makes patching more accurate, as well as granular - feasible amount of patches is automatically adapted for the particular SOC/SDK/OEM case, building a solid foundation.
### UserOptions (UO)
Useroptions were overhauled in SILMARIL. Expanded with more flags to experiment with and have a broader space for personal tinkering, whether universally, or for particular platform. Various UO lags were crosslinked with one-another, as well as with internal dynamic installer logic to offer a more robust experience. Additionally, debugging section added to provide comprehensive way to iterate through problematic installations.
### Connectivity
SILMARIL's variable patching approach opens up ability to support various playback connectivity types, including: internal speakers, usb-c, bluetooth and legacy 3.5 jack.
### AINULINDALE v2
With AINULINDALE at its core, SILMARIL aims at eradicating the long lasting issue of android's forced up/down sampling bottleneck. By looping input rate to the output it effectively sets 1:1 native sampling for the OS and third-party apps that rely on it. Next, to make sampling fully transparent it increases temporal domain resolution by expanding the number of discrete points. This firmly secures signal's characteristics and transients, while exponentially dialing down quantization errors, phase distortion, temporal smearing & aliasing artifacts. Additionally, AINULINDALE improves buffer & memory allocation and switches sampler to UHQ state, getting rid of throttling jitter during FIR gen.
The second-generation AINULINDALE engine redefines Android's audio pipeline at the system level, replacing core processing stages with mathematically refined implementations designed to preserve precision from decoding to final output. Every component is engineered to minimize numerical error, maintain phase integrity, and deliver a transparent, natural presentation that stays faithful to the original recording.:
> Custom Double-Precision Bessel by James34602
>
> A custom double-precision Bessel implementation replaces the original truncated approximation used during FIR coefficient generation. By converging to machine precision, the Kaiser window is generated with significantly lower numerical error, producing more accurate filter coefficients and improved stop-band performance for cleaner resampling.
>
> High-Fidelity DC-Blocking
>
> A real-time single-pole DC blocker removes DC offset immediately after integer-to-float conversion across every supported PCM format. Internal double-precision filter states preserve long-term accuracy while an ultra-low cutoff frequency maintains complete transparency throughout the audible spectrum, including the deepest sub-bass.
>
> TPDF Dither Engine
>
> A mathematically correct TPDF dither engine combined with second-order noise shaping minimizes correlated quantization distortion during bit-depth reduction. Dither energy is shifted toward ultrasonic frequencies, allowing low-level detail and ambience to remain perceptually intact without introducing harsh digital artifacts.
>
> Deferred Gain Staging
>
> Instead of attenuating audio before processing, SILMARIL maintains unity gain throughout the DSP pipeline and applies user volume only at the final rendering stage. Preserving full internal signal resolution allows subsequent processing to operate with maximum numerical precision while reducing rounding error during low-volume playback.
>
> Soft-Saturation Limiter
>
> A true-peak-aware limiter uses 2x oversampling with polyphase interpolation to detect inter-sample peaks before they reach the output stage. Audio below the limiting threshold passes transparently, while genuine overshoots are controlled using a smooth saturation curve that avoids the harsh artifacts associated with conventional brickwall limiting.

Installation
- Flash module with Magisk(Delta/Kitsune)/KernelSU/KernelSUNext/APatch/SukiSU app. With ever growing number of roots/metamodules as well as their forks, along with frequent changes to their core logic - some root/mounting solutions might not work correctly.
- Initial install will place UserOptions file to internal storage. To experiment with extra options open silmaril_useroptions as text and follow instructions on what flags supposed to do and which values used. :exclamation: Reinstalling the module is vital for changes to take any effect. It is advised to uninstall & reinstall module, instead of flashing it over for some cases.

Troubleshooting
In case experiencing any bugs - navigate to UserOptions's Debug Section can be found. Follow its instructions to resolve the issue.

- Tech Kush Channel @ Telegram
- Ainur Audio @ XDA-Developers

- MMT-Ex Template
- XMLStarlet

- ✅ Full uninstall restoration for settings, properties, and services
- ✅ Better reversibility (returns closer to pre-install state)
- ✅ Improved uninstall logging (/data/local/tmp/ghostgms_uninstall.log)
- ✅ Core + Legacy lines both maintained

🛠️ What Gets Optimized?

📊 Categories
- 🛑 Ads & tracking: Reduces ad ID usage and background tracking hooks
- 📈 Analytics & reporting: Limits telemetry and passive reporting behavior
- 🔄 Background/update behavior: Cuts unnecessary background churn and update checks
- 📍 Location/geofence components: Restricts extra location polling and geofence overhead
- 📡 Nearby/discovery services: Trims nearby device discovery/casting activity
- ☁️ Sync/cloud extras: Keeps core sync while reducing non-essential cloud operations
- 💳 Wallet/payment-related services: Disables payment components if you do not use them
- ⌚ Wear/fitness integrations: Reduces wearable and fitness service wakeups

⚙️ Installation

1. Download from Releases
2. Flash in Magisk
3. Pick Core or Legacy module
4. Select optimization presets/options
5. Reboot and let the system settle

🔋 Battery Behavior After Install

You might see temporary drain for 24–48 hours while Android re-calibrates background behavior.
That is expected; battery results usually improve after the settling phase.

🚫 What It Does *Not* Do

❓ Troubleshooting

If notifications, Play Store installs/updates, account sync, and app sign-in are working normally, this warning is usually safe to ignore.

Push notifications feel delayed

modules.name: ReSuSFS
modules.author: ahmed-alnassif
modules.description: SuSFS for KernelSU (Built-in & LKM Supported) | Strong Hiding by Default | Powerful UserHub Script Manager with Scheduling | Clean Configs & Toggles
modules.readme:
ReSuSFS

Root hiding made simple, powerful when you need it. A KernelSU module and WebUI that turns SuSFS into clean config files and toggle switches for everyday use, with strong hiding applied out of the box via built-in spoofing and hiding scripts for one-tap protection, plus a script manager with scheduling for power users who want more, all without leaving the WebUI.
[!Important]
KernelSU Next is not recommended.
KernelSU Next is currently unmaintained and has been observed engaging in anti-competitive behavior, including blacklisting the official ReSuSFS module without technical justification. This is not a security decision, it is a control decision.
Using an unmaintained kernel root solution can lead to:
- Instability and unexpected crashes.
- Bootloops that can leave your device unusable.
- Security vulnerabilities that will never be patched.
- Broken module compatibility as the ecosystem moves forward.
To protect your device and ensure you receive official support:
- Use KernelSU: The upstream, official root solution.
- Use BakaSU: A trusted, community-respected fork.
ReSuSFS is the only official SuSFS module for KernelSU. It is fully supported on KernelSU and BakaSU only.
Do not use KernelSU Next. Choose stability. Choose freedom. Choose official support.
[!Important]
Future Direction
ReSuSFS will gradually move beyond SuSFS management. SuSFS will become optional, while development will focus more on UserHub, giving users greater freedom and control to create, manage, and automate their own scripts and configurations.

Requirements
- KernelSU
- SuSFS support is optional, pick one:
- GKID Kernel with SuSFS built in
- A supported GKI kernel, ReSuSFS loads the SuSFS LKM for you (see SuSFS LKM)

Install

1. Download the latest release
2. Flash the zip in KernelSU Manager
3. Reboot (a full reboot is required after installing or updating, hot install is not supported)
4. Strong hiding is applied automatically, no setup needed
5. Optional: edit config files, or use the WebUI to fine-tune

When updating, ReSuSFS asks before touching your existing configs, and only asks for a backup if configs exist.
[!Note]
v26.10.16 removed hidden_api_policy so ReSuSFS no longer enables hidden API access. If you edited your configuration before, review it after updating.

Config files

All optional, all live under /data/adb/ReSuSFS/. Missing or empty files mean "nothing to apply" for that feature, no errors. Entries are appended in the order they appear, top line first.

| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| sus_paths.txt | hide static/read-only paths |
| sus_paths_loop.txt | hide frequently changing paths |
| sus_maps.txt | hide mapped library files |
| kstat_paths.txt | spoof file stat for bind mounted paths |
| open_redirect.txt | redirect a path to another path |
| uname.txt | spoof kernel release/version |
| cmdline_or_bootconfig.txt | spoof /proc/cmdline or /proc/bootconfig |
| config.txt | toggle kernel flags (mount hiding, logging, avc spoofing) |
| scripts/ | built-in scripts for spoofing and hiding |
| scripts_postfs.txt | scripts to run at post-fs-data stage |
| scripts_bootcompleted.txt | scripts to run at boot-completed stage |
| scripts_cron.txt | scheduled scripts and their cron expressions |
| cron.log | start time, end time, and exit code of every scheduled run |

SuSFS LKM

Kernels without built-in SuSFS (CONFIG_KSU_SUSFS=y) can still use it through the SuSFS guard LKM from susfs4ksu-lkm.
- Detected automatically from your kernel, nothing to configure
- Downloaded when you flash the module or run Action
- Loaded on every boot at post-fs-data
- Skipped when your kernel already has SuSFS built in

Supported KMIs: android12-5.10, android13-5.10, android13-5.15, android14-5.15, android14-6.1, android15-6.6, android16-6.12, android17-6.18. Custom kernels with a different KMI are not supported.

Files are stored in /data/adb/ReSuSFS_LKM/. If the download fails, ReSuSFS keeps the version you already have.

Built-in Scripts

Pre-made scripts for common spoofing and hiding tasks. They live in /data/adb/ReSuSFS/scripts/ and are enabled by default for set-and-forget users. They can be disabled by removing their filenames from scripts_postfs.txt or scripts_bootcompleted.txt.

Strong hiding is applied out of the box with no configuration needed. Power users can fine-tune individual scripts via the WebUI or by editing the files directly.

| Script | Stage | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| ReSuSFS_apply-cmdline-bootconfig.sh | post-fs-data | hides bootloader unlock state from kernel cmdline/bootconfig |
| ReSuSFS_apply-kstat-add.sh | post-fs-data | hides file stats for framework-managed paths |
| ReSuSFS_apply-ksu-settings.sh | post-fs-data | sets KernelSU features for hiding and compatibility |
| ReSuSFS_apply-uname.sh | post-fs-data | spoofs kernel version and build info from uname |
| ReSuSFS_apply-mount-hiding.sh | boot-completed | hides module mounts redirected to system paths |
| ReSuSFS_apply-props.sh | boot-completed | spoofs root indicators and removes custom ROM fingerprints |
| ReSuSFS_apply-settings.sh | boot-completed | spoofs developer options and debugging states in system settings |
| ReSuSFS_apply-sus-maps.sh | boot-completed | hides zygisk libraries and module font files from memory maps |
| ReSuSFS_apply-sus-paths-loop.sh | boot-completed | hides recovery traces, root tools, and suspicious pty nodes |
| ReSuSFS_apply-sus-paths.sh | boot-completed | hides custom ROM traces and addon.d paths |
| ReSuSFS_cleanup-markers.sh | boot-completed | removes susfs leftover markers from shared storage |

WebUI Features
- Strong hiding by default, built-in scripts are pre-enabled for set-and-forget users
- Status dashboard, see if SuSFS is active at a glance, tap for the full enabled-features breakdown straight from the kernel
- Configuration summary, live entry counts per feature and enabled script count, right on the home page...

modules.name: DNSCrypt-Proxy 2
modules.author: d3cim
modules.description: A flexible DNS proxy, with support for modern encrypted DNS protocols such as DNSCrypt v2, DNS-over-HTTPS, Anonymized DNSCrypt and ODoH (Oblivious DoH). Using dnscrypt-proxy 2.1.5
modules.readme:
DNSCrypt Proxy 2 for Android

A flexible DNS proxy, with support for modern encrypted DNS protocols such as DNSCrypt v2, DNS-over-HTTPS, Anonymized DNSCrypt and ODoH (Oblivious DoH).

Features
- For all features please refer to the official page.

Pre-built binaries

Up-to-date, pre-built binaries are available for:
- Android/arm
- Android/arm64
- Android/x86
- Android/x86_64

All the binary files are downloaded from the official release page.

Differences from the main project
- server_names = ams-dnscrypt-nl [NLD], d0wn-tz-ns1 [TZA], dct-nl [NLD], dct-ru [RUS], dnscrypt.be [BEL], dnscrypt.pl [POL], dnscrypt.uk-ipv4 [GBR], dnswarden-uncensor-dc-swiss [CHE], meganerd [NLD], openinternet [USA], plan9dns-fl [USA], plan9dns-mx [MEX], plan9dns-nj [USA], pryv8boi [DEU], sby-limotelu [IDN], scaleway-ams [NLD], scaleway-fr [FRA], serbica [NLD], techsaviours.org-dnscrypt [DEU], v.dnscrypt.uk-ipv4 [GBR] are the resolvers in use.
- doh_servers = false (disable servers implementing the DNS-over-HTTPS protocol)
- require_dnssec = true (server must support DNSSEC security extension)
- force_tcp = true (fix for mobile data intial connection random issues if routes have been set and skip_incompatible = true, see DNSCrypt/dnscrypt-proxy/discussions/2020)
- timeout = 1000 (set the max. response time of a single DNS query from 5000 to 1000 ms.)
- blocked_query_response = 'refused' (set refused response to blocked queries)
- # log_level = 0 (set the log level of the dnscrypt-proxy.log file to very verbose, but keep it disabled by default)
- dnscrypt_ephemeral_keys = true (create a new, unique key for every single DNS query)
- bootstrap_resolvers = ['45.11.45.11:53'] (use DNS.SB instead CloudFlare)
- netprobe_address = '45.11.45.11:53' (use DNS.SB instead CloudFlare)
- block_ipv6 = true (immediately respond to IPv6-related queries with an empty response)
- blocked-names.txt, blocked-ips.txt, allowed-names.txt and allowed-ips.txt files enabled. (to know more specifics about this, please refer to the Filters (optional) section below)
- anonymized_dns feature enabled. (routes are indirect ways to reach DNSCrypt servers, each resolver has 2 relays assigned)
- skip_incompatible = true (skip resolvers incompatible with anonymization instead of using them directly)
- direct_cert_fallback = false (prevent direct connections through the resolvers for failed certificate retrieved via relay)

Installation

1. Download the latest dnscrypt-proxy-android-*.zip file from the Releases page and flash it with Magisk:

Magisk > Modules > Install from storage > dnscrypt-proxy-android-*.zip

2. Reboot your device.

3. Test your DNS at https://dnsleaktest.com/

Configuration (optional)

You can edit the dnscrypt-proxy.toml file as you wish located on storage/emulated/0/dnscrypt-proxy path.

For a more detailed configuration you can refer to the official documentation or simply join our group on Telegram, at dnscrypt-proxy-android | CHAT.

Filters (optional)

Filters are a powerful set of built-in features, that let you control exactly what domain names and IP addresses your device are allowed to connect to. This can be used to block ads, trackers, malware, or anything you don't want your device to load.

This module comes with the filtering feature enabled by default, that's why you can see files designed for this operation inside the internal folder. Out of the box these files are empty and are used only to ensure the correct start of dnscrypt-proxy service.\
To know more about it you can consult the official documentation, or in a simpler way through my block repository.

I'm also providing the allowed-names.txt and blocked-names.txt files regularly updated at dnscrypt-proxy-filters | CHANNEL. The sources used for this merge are among the hardest on the web.

You can contribute to this blocklist at anytime, opening a New Issue here or simply reporting the issue at dnscrypt-proxy-filters | CHAT on Telegram.

Changelog
- See CHANGELOG.

Version numbers

dnscrypt-proxy-android tags follow the format {dnscrypt-proxy_version}.{revision} where
- dnscrypt-proxy_version is the version of dnscrypt-proxy used in x.x.x format, and
- revision is a number indicating the version of dnscrypt-proxy-android for the corresponding dnscrypt-proxy version.

modules.author: lok1s
modules.description: Enables Quick Share mosey AirDrop transport on Pixel 8 Pro and other non-Pixel-10 devices via Phenotype injection + MoseyApp reinstall
modules.readme:
This project is independent and not affiliated with, authorized, or endorsed by Google LLC or Apple Inc.
All trademarks (including Android, Google, and AirDrop) belong to their respective owners.

HELP WANTED! ПРОЕКТУ НУЖНА ПОМОЩЬ!
If you own (or know someone who owns) Pixel 9 or Pixel 10 series device (excluding 9a) or any other device that supports Airdrop (Galaxy S24-26, some BBK devices) and willing to help this project – proceed to AIRDROP TESTING GUIDE

Если у вас (или ваших знакомых) есть Pixel 9/10 (не считая 9a) или любое другое устройство поддерживающее Airdrop (Galaxy S24-26, пара устройств от BBK) и желание помочь проекту – прочтите ГАЙД ПО ТЕСТИРОВАНИЮ AIRDROP

Mosey Extended v2 (MMT-Ex)

  English · Русский

English

EXPERIMENTAL AND IN ACTIVE DEVELOPMENT!

FLASH ANY MODULES AT YOUR OWN RISK! You MUST know exactly what you are doing.
For research and debugging purposes only.

Table of Contents

1. What is this?
2. How AirDrop (mosey) works — full stack
3. Full modification tree
4. Supported devices & Wi-Fi modems
5. Key files location table
6. Current status
7. Build: wonder\_mosey\_wild.ko
8. Deployment & service.sh integration
9. Known limitations

1. What is this?

A few weeks ago, I reverse-engineered a Pixel 10 firmware image and identified
the missing component required to enable AirDrop-style functionality in Google
Quick Share on older Pixel devices — and potentially any Android device.

I found a native binary named mosey_server (matching the APK extension
component for Quick Share). Static analysis shows it is a native Android
service, not a CLI tool. It links against libbinder_ndk.so, liblog.so,
libc.so, and libdl.so, and contains the string
AServiceManager_addService. The embedded source path
vendor/google/services/QuickShareExtension/src/server.rs confirms it is part
of the Quick Share extension and is expected to start at boot.

The binary attempts to register a native AIDL (NDK Binder) service via
AServiceManager_addService("com.google.pixel.service.IService/default").

Initial attempts to inject and run this binary via KSU module failed because:
1. AServiceManager_addService() requires more than just SELinux allow rules.
2. The service name must be mapped to a valid SELinux service type in
   vendor_service_contexts.
3. Without that mapping, registration fails with PERMISSION_DENIED or
   UNKNOWN_ERROR.

The Pixel 10 vendor image includes all required components. This project
transplants them — along with a virtual "wonder" Wi-Fi phy — so that
mosey_server can run on any rooted Android device.

2. How AirDrop (mosey) works — full stack

Google's "AirDrop" (internal codename mosey) in Quick Share requires a
specific Wi-Fi interface named wonder to be present on the device. The
mosey_server native service communicates with this interface through the
Linux cfg80211/nl80211 subsystem.

The full boot sequence:

Boot
 └─ init parses mosey.rc
     └─ starts mosey_server (NET_ADMIN, NET_RAW caps)
         ├─ registers "com.google.pixel.service.IService/default" with servicemanager
         ├─ sends NL80211_CMD_NEW_INTERFACE to create "wonder0" (MONITOR mode)
         ├─ sets channel 149 / 5745 MHz via NL80211_CMD_SET_CHANNEL
         ├─ sends NL80211 vendor commands (vendor_id=0x1A11):
         │   ├─ subcmd 1: set_frequency
         │   ├─ subcmd 2: set_filter
         │   ├─ subcmd 3: set_fixed_tx_rate
         │   ├─ subcmd 4: set_reg
         │   └─ subcmd 5: get_if_mac_addr → reads 6-byte MAC
         └─ opens PF_PACKET / TPACKET_V3 on wonder0 for 802.11 frame I/O

On Pixel 9 / 10, this chain works natively via the BCM4398 chip's
wondertap mechanism inside bcmdhd. On older Pixels (7/8) and non-Pixel
devices, this project provides the missing pieces:
- wonder_mosey_wild.ko — a standalone virtual mac80211 driver that
  creates the wonder phy and handles all vendor commands natively.
- SELinux policy — extracted from Pixel 10, injected via KSU sepolicy.rule.
- mosey.rc — init service definition, overlaid via KSU module.

3. Full modification tree

The following tree lists every layer that must be modified or provided to
bring AirDrop online, from high-level feature flags down to the modem driver.
Items marked ✅ are handled by this module; ⚠️ indicates partial / in-progress;
❌ indicates not yet implemented.

modules.name: Noogle microG Catfish
modules.author: SelfRef
modules.description: Replaces Google Services with microG, no signature spoofing needed
modules.readme:
noogle-magisk

Magisk modules for removing/replacing Google applications on stock Android 11-17.

Noogle is developed in my free time. If it helps you get rid of Google, consider supporting its development:

Modules

Name | Description
--- | ---
Noogle microG | Installs microG Services in place of Google Services (if present), comes in 4 variants
Noogle Unbundle | Removes other Google apps from system, comes in 3 variants

Modules are independent, use one or both. Variants of a module replace each other, switch anytime by installing another variant over the installed one, the installer brings back or removes apps as needed.

Which Noogle microG to choose

Variant | Play Store | Signature spoofing | microG updates from F-Droid | Play Integrity Fix
:--- | --- | --- | --- | ---
noogle-microg | Replaced by microG Companion | Needed | Yes | Yes
noogle-microg-playful | Kept * | Needed | Yes | Yes
noogle-microg-catfish | Replaced by microG Companion | Not needed | No | microG may crash
noogle-microg-playful-catfish | Kept * | Not needed | No | microG may crash

Playful or not: Playful keeps Play Store of your ROM. The others replace it with microG Companion, which only provides Play Store services to apps, use Aurora Store to get apps.

Catfish or not: Regular variants need your ROM to report Google's signature for microG (signature spoofing), which stock Android can't do without Vector and FakeGApps. Catfish microG carries signing blocks copied from Google's APKs instead. Android doesn't check contents of system apps against their signatures, so it reports Google's signature without any spoofing. Idea from microG_no_sigspoof by IsHacker. The downsides:
- Signatures don't match the contents, so Catfish APKs can't be installed as user apps: microG updates come only with the module (switching to Catfish removes ones installed from F-Droid), and Play Integrity Fix workaround (microG installed as user updates) isn't possible
- Google's updates of Play Services pass as valid updates, the module removes them on every boot
- Tested on Android 15 emulator so far

If your ROM already supports signature spoofing (see ROMs), use a regular variant.

Which Noogle Unbundle to choose

Variant | Removes | Kept | List
:--- | --- | --- | ---
noogle-unbundle | Google apps installable from store: Chrome, Gmail, Maps, YouTube, Photos, Drive, Google app... | Phone basics, accessibility, Google system components | packages.txt
noogle-unbundle-hard | Same, plus phone basics (Pixel Launcher, Phone, Messages, Gboard, Camera, Clock, Contacts...), accessibility (TalkBack, Speech Services), Google system components (Android System Intelligence, Digital Wellbeing, Android Auto...) and Pixel extras | Setup Wizard, Device Health Services, Network Stack, file and sound pickers, carrier services and others that break the phone when removed (tested) | packages.txt + packages-hard.txt
noogle-unbundle-fossify | Same as Hard, and installs Fossify apps as replacements | Same as Hard | Same as Hard

They never remove apps Noogle microG replaces. Switching from Hard or Fossify to a lighter variant brings back apps removed only by them.

Fossify: installs Launcher, Phone, Messages, Keyboard, Contacts, Gallery, Calculator, Clock, Camera, File Manager, Calendar, Notes and Voice Recorder as system apps. They are the versions from F-Droid (Fossify's own reproducible builds), so F-Droid updates them, updates stay installed even after removing the module. On every boot the module switches to Fossify Keyboard when the keyboard in use is gone (also on lock screen, so you can type your password), and gives empty home, phone and SMS roles to Fossify apps. Other Fossify apps (Music Player, Paint, Documents...) are in F-Droid.

Hard removes apps your phone may have no other one for. Install and set up replacements before installing it: launcher, phone, SMS app, camera, clock with alarms, and a keyboard enabled in settings (without one you can't type your password). The installer keeps apps with no replacement installed (it shows them as KEPT), install the module again after adding replacements. Contacts, Gallery or Calculator are removed without checks, install your own if you need them. Open your clock and calendar once and allow notifications, otherwise alarms ring with nothing on screen to stop them and reminders don't show. On some phones alarms of any app may go silent without Google Clock, check yours rings after installing. Fossify variant brings its own replacements and allows notifications for Fossify Clock and Calendar, but the alarm warning applies too.

Install

It requires Magisk v29.0 or newer. If you don't have it yet, consult the official installation instructions.

It's a good idea to enable ADB debugging as well before installing in case of any issues.

KernelSU and APatch are supported too, but tested less than Magisk. Recent versions (KernelSU v3.0+, APatch 11219+) need a metamodule installed first (e.g. meta-overlayfs or NoMount, which one works best depends on the device), otherwise the module files are not mounted. On KernelSU disable "Umount modules" in App Profile of microG Services, microG Companion and Services Framework Proxy.

Modules are mainly tested on Android emulators (Google Play images). Real devices and vendor ROMs may behave differently, please report any issues you hit.

1. Download variant of your choice from releases
- For playful variant on ROMs without Play Store see playful build
- Noogle Unbundle is optional and works on its own, install it as a separate module
2. Install through Magisk app
3. Reboot, microG permissions are granted automatically on first boot
4. Ensure all permission boxes are checked in microG Self-Check
- If not, click "Action" button next to module in Magisk to grant them again, or tap them in Self-Check
5. Check signature spoofing status at the top of Self-Check
- Regular variants on ROMs without signature spoofing: add it
6...

SAM
SAM 是 SmartDNS、AdGuardHome 和 Mihomo 三合一的 Magisk 模块。每一个服务都可以单独使用，或者两两组合，或者全部启用。

📖说明
- SmartDNS 的优先级最低，在无启用其它服务的情况下，才会作为本机的 DNS 转发服务，在有两种和三种服务启用，只会作为上游 DNS。
- AdGuardHome 在单独启用和 SmartDNS 一起使用，都会作为本机的 DNS 转发服务，再和 Mihomo 三种一起用，就根据设置文件的配置，来选择使用哪种结构。
- Mihomo 在单独使用，或者和另一种服务使用，都会作为本机的 DNS 转发服务。

⚙️功能
- 两种服务结构:
- SmartDNS > Mihomo > AdGuardHome
- SmartDNS > AdGuardHome > Mihomo
- 监听:
- 模块:
- 启用即运行，禁用即停止
- 卸载备份配置，恢复拦截广告
- hosts:
- 修改实时生效
- 黑名单 WIFI 配置
- 黑白名单代理 App 配置
- 定时执行

📢注意
- 禁止和其它同类型模块使用
- 模块所有服务的账号和密码都是 root
- 禁止该文件随意修改
- /data/adb/modules/SAM/etc/mihomo/base.yaml

⚠️无网络
- 检查手机网络，开关飞行模式
- 排查 Mihomo 和 AdGuardHome 的拦截日志，手动添加规则放行

🤝使用项目
- MetaCubeX/mihomo
- vernesong/mihomo

🙏感谢

modules.author: eventlOwOp
modules.description: zerotier for magisk
modules.readme:
ZeroTier for Magisk

[中文 | English]

Run zerotier in the background after booting!

No conflicts with other Android VPN service!

Use Android App to control ZeroTier

Support for Private Root Servers

Requirements

1. a version is built with Android NDK Toolchain, supporting api 28 (Android 9.0) and above.

2. another version is build with GCC toolchain, linking to Linux Syscalls statically

Unofficial planet supported; SSO (zeroidc) supported in the version built with GCC for AArch64

AArch64 suppots ARMv8-A and above; Arm version supports ARMv7-A (compiling with -march=armv7-a)

Installation

1. Download magisk module zip file from github release; install.
2. Download controller app apk file from github release; install.
3. Reboot your phone.
4. Open controller app; enter your 16-character network id; join.
5. Enjoy 😋

Usage

Use Private Root Servers

Replace /data/adb/zerotier/home/planet with your own planet file.

Controller App

Does not need root privilege

| Feature            | Supported? |
| :----------------- | :--------- |
| status             | ✅         |
| start/stop         | ✅         |
| join/leave network | ✅         |
| join/leave planet  | ❎         |

Command line tools

Use zerotier.sh to start/stop or inspect status.

Usage: zerotier.sh {start|stop|restart|status}

Use zerotier-cli / zerotier-idtool for ZeroTierOne command line operations.

(zerotier-one not copied to /system/bin)

Files

/data/adb/zerotier
├── home                                    # zerotier-one home directory
│   ├── authtoken.secret                    # zerotier-one http interface authtoken
│   ├── zerotier-one.pid                    # zerotier-one pid
│   ├── zerotier-one.port                   # zerotier-one port
│   └── ...
├── lib                                     # only in NDK compiled module
│   └── libc++_shared.so                    # NDK dynamic library
├── run
│   ├── daemon.log                          # service.sh log
│   ├── pipe                                # named pipe to interact with service.sh
│   ├── zerotier.log                        # zerotier-one log
│   └── ...
├── zerotier-cli -> zerotier-one            # zerotier-one command line interface
├── zerotier-idtool -> zerotier-one         # zerotier-one id tool
├── zerotier-one                            # zerotier-one executable
└── zerotier.sh

all the scripts and binaries are placed in /data/adb/zerotier/, and all copied to /system/bin (in PATH) to be executed directly (except zerotier-one)

zerotier.sh uses named pipe to communicate with service.sh, preventing ZeroTier to start as a subprocess of Shell.

log files are placed in run, daemon.log for service.sh and zerotier.log for ZeroTierOne.

Build binaries yourself

refer to .github/workflow/build-{gcc|ndk}.yml for detailed information.

Notes

After 1.14.0, ZeroTierOne has introduce multi-core concurrent packet processing, which requires pthread_setaffinity_np.

However, for NDK, pthread_setaffinity_np won't be available until API level 36, Android 16. (refer to https://android.googlesource.com/platform/bionic/+/master/libc/include/pthread.h)

So in the NDK bulid version, it is replaced by the combination of pthread_gettid_np from  and sched_getaffinity from .

Using your phone as router, want LAN to LAN mapping?

See ThermalEng/zerotier-magisk. Inform me by creating issue. Future function and UI integration if many module users want it.

modules.name: AZenith火
modules.author: ArchHaven Developers
modules.description: One, Two, Three! AZenith has arrived!
modules.readme:
Overview

AZenith is an All-In-One (AIO) Universal Performance module for
Android — built to work across devices and ROMs, and designed to
respect your preferences: nothing is forced, every tweak is opt-in and
stays fully under your control.

It pairs two Rust daemons with a Material 3 Expressive manager app:
archdaemon (profiles, bypass charging, FPS Recorder) and
sysdaemon (pure-binder app monitor + FPS client). Together they
auto-switch performance profiles when a game runs, tune kernel
scheduling, record real frametime stats, and put an in-game Game Space
overlay on screen — without shell-forking in the hot path.

Features

Game Space

A landscape, gamepad-first shell built on Material 3 Expressive —
smooth, playful UI with spring animations, dynamic colors and
notification-style cards. Launched from the manager, then handed over
to the overlay service for the rest of the session. Designed for
gamepad users: D-Pad / joystick navigation, A select, B back, L1/R1
switch tab, no touch required.
- Perfect dashboard in one place — game library tiles, app tiles,
  spotlight, BGM playlist with now-playing controls, wallpapers,
  status trophies, battery, service PID, games tracked, FPS, CPU/GPU
  load and temps all on one landscape screen
- Ambient music — customizable BGM playlist (shuffle / repeat /
  sequential) with volume control and long-press quick actions
- Fun interface — expressive shapes, dynamic Material You
  theming, spring micro-animations, boot hand-off sequence
  (linking, scan, tune, ready), quick toggles for profile,
  refresh rate and tweaks
- Settings: appearance (sidepanel side / sensitivity / length /
  thickness / opacity / blur, custom images), audio, general (boost
  on launch, renderer, refresh rate, frame-rate target, resolution
  downscale), tweaks (FPSGO, GED, WAL, SFL, thermal, scheduler),
  and About
- Floating app windows on top of the game (open from inside the shell)
- Crosshair reticle overlay

Sidepanel + FPS Monitor

Edge-bar + expandable Material 3 Expressive dock — every control
you need lives right inside the game: profile switch, battery, temps
and framerate without ever leaving the session.
- Handle bar (swipe-in to expand, vertical drag to reposition,
  configurable length/thickness/side) — shown only for games in your
  configured list, app-lunch list, or when force-sidepanel is on
- In-game access control — switch profile, check battery and
  temps, and watch framerate live, all from the dock
- FPS Meter with small FPS badge flush left of the number,
  frame time (1000 / fps ms) and estimated 1% Low
- FPS Recorder — one-tap Start / Stop (record pill with ripple,
  session timer); writes CSV + JSON summaries with real ft_avg /
  ft_max / low1 / low01 / jank from the frametime histogram
- Customizable layout — widgets (FPS, CPU, GPU, temp, ping,
  battery, profile) with HUD offsets, global + per-app layouts
- Floating apps — open other apps in floating windows on top of
  the game from inside the dock
- Quick Apps row, brightness/volume sliders, auto-mode toggle,
  profile switcher, toasts

Per-App Tuning

Per-app tweaks override every global setting for the selected game —
set each parameter once per game and it applies on game focus,
falling back to the global values otherwise:
- Per-app Lite Mode (cap at ~90% CPU freq, mid-frequency ladder)
- Per-app rendering (renderer override: default / SkiaVulkan /
  SkiaGLES / software)
- Per-app refresh rate (target from the device's mode list)
- Per-app downscaler (resolution downscale 0–100% + target FPS slider)
- Per-app DND (do-not-disturb during gaming)
- App Priority (process priority boost)
- Game Preload (libs + page-cache preload, with budget)
- Resolution downscale badge always shows the live divider

_(Display config is not per-app — there is no per-app display filter.)_

Profiles

AZenith switches profile automatically depending on what you need —
gaming in foreground → Performance, battery saver on → ECO,
everything else → Balanced (with a 10 s screen-off grace and 30 s
foreground-away grace before dropping back).

You can also take manual control: turn off Auto Mode in Settings
and pick Performance, Balanced or ECO yourself whenever
you want.

Custom Governor

AZenith lets you set a custom CPU governor per profile — pick
your own governor for Performance, Balanced and ECO instead of the
stock defaults:
- Custom CPU governor per profile (custom_*_cpu_gov)
- Custom I/O scheduler per profile (custom_*_IO)
- Custom Mali GPU governor per profile (custom_*_maligpu_gov)
- Stock defaults stay untouched unless you override them; balanced
  can also restore the saved baseline governor
- disabletweak master switch

Thermalcore

Intelligent thermal throttling — watches CPU/GPU temps and adapts
limits so you hold a stable FPS floor instead of thermal-crashing.

Bypass Charging

Built-in bypass charging for supported devices:
- Diagnostic check that tests whether your device actually supports
  the feature before enabling it
- Adjustable charging threshold to match your battery health usage
- Charging-state dynamic bypass while gaming

Preference Tweaks

AZenith ships extra add-on tweaks you can enable or disable whenever
you like — flip each one on/off from the tweaks screen and it applies
immediately:
- schedtunes, WALT tunes
- FPSGO & GED parameters (MediaTek), Mali scheduler
- SFL latency, display colour presets

Installation

Magisk module — install through your root manager (KernelSU /
Magisk):

1. Flash the release zip.
2. Reboot.
3. Enjoy

For Developers (ROM Integration)

ROM-Integrated AZenith: system-level service for custom ROMs —
single vendor.azenith-service binary, AIDL interface, init rc,
sepolicy. See the
RomIntegratedAZenith
repository.

Contributing & Bug Reports

We welcome contributions!
- Report Bugs: open an issue with a log.
- Feature Requests: open an issue to discuss.
- Pull Requests: fork, create a branch, submit a PR with a clear
  description.

Credits & Acknowledgements...

modules.name: Nfqttl
modules.author: Cyborg-one
modules.description: Nfqttl is a module fix heder field ttl. github: https://github.com/cyborg-one/nfqttl
modules.readme:
Nfqttl
- Nfqttl - module for modifying the ttl value in the packet header.
- Sets the ttl value of 64 for the packet on the mobile data interface and sets the ttl value of 65 for the packet on the local interface (wifi, bluetooth).
- Splitting the tcp packet into sequences.
- For incoming packets, if ttl = 1, set to ttl 64.
- IPv6 packets are dropped.

How to use
- Download and install from storage in Magisk App the installing archive:
nfqttl2.1.2.zip.
- Reboot.
- When device boots, Magisk will start the module.

How it work
- The networking subsystem of the Linux kernel has a mechanism to pass network packets to the user
application for processing (NetFilter Queue). Nfqttl receives packets, edits the ttl packet header fields and the checksum,
and sends them back to the kernel.

Compatibility
- Magisk 20.4+
- Nfqueue

Links
- GitHub repository Magisk module
- GitHub repository source code
